title: Quarterly product runway: Hosted endpoints prioritization & model lifecycle gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized, executable quarterly runway that (1) defines which hosted endpoints to promote or deprecate this quarter, (2) establishes model lifecycle gating criteria for new model variants, and (3) codifies canary and rollback policies to avoid quality regressions. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, Design, and Research deliverables required to land the plan and the first tranche of endpoint releases.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints (text generation/chat/embeddings) across the public catalog and reserved hosted tiers. Excludes Dedicated-only infra changes except where they affect routing and fallback policies.

Out-of-scope: On-prem packaging and legal contract negotiation for enterprise customers (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ranked list of endpoint releases and deprecations with owner, required infra changes, and risk score.
2) Written gating checklist for onboarding model variants (evaluation thresholds, latency/cost budget, K-anonymized safety checks).
3) Canary schedule and rollback playbook uploaded to Confluence with runbook links.
4) Cross-team signoff (Eng, Design, Research, SRE, Security).
5) First canary rollout for top-priority endpoint initiated and metrics captured for two full weeks.
success_metrics:
- Percent of endpoint releases that meet quality gates in first canary: >= 90%
- No critical customer regressions in first 4 weeks post-release
- Median p50 latency change < +10ms and p99 within SLO
- Unit inference cost variance < 7% versus baseline

dependencies_notes: Primary engineering dependencies: kernel scheduling change in ENG-8127 (affects latency under batching), KV cache enhancement in ENG-8391 for warm-start perf. Design dependency DES-214 for endpoint UX/consumption docs. Security to vet KMS/HSM interactions for model keys. Research to provide evaluation suite and baseline prompts (linked below).
decisions: Favor promoting smaller, well-characterized model variants (quantized 8-bit) for public hosted endpoints to control cost and latency.
Adopt two-tier gating: automated eval thresholds + human review for safety-sensitive endpoints.
Regional canaries will default to 5% traffic in primary region, 1% in secondary before global promotion.
risks: Model quality regressions detected only in niche customer prompts not covered by eval suite
Kernel/inference runtime regressions from ENG-8127 that could increase p99 latency
Insufficient canary traffic leading to inconclusive metrics
Compliance review slip causing delayed promotion for regulated customers
mitigations: Expand eval prompt set using telemetry-derived examples and surface gaps weekly
Coordinate synchronized rollout with runtime feature flags to disable new kernels quickly
Plan canary windows around predictable traffic cycles and include synthetic load tests
Engage Security early; include compliance checklist in gating criteria
